doc:
At each point during the search, every node of the tree (goal, rapp or mvar
cluster) is in one of these states:

- `proven`: the node is proven.
- `unprovable`: the node is unprovable, i.e. it will never be proven regardless
  of any future expansions that might be performed.
- `unknown`: neither of the above.

Every node starts in the `unknown` state and may later become either `proven` or
`unprovable`. After this, the state does not change any more.

doc: Insert a forward rule into the `ForwardIndex`.

signature.text: def Aesop.ForwardIndex.insert (r : Aesop.ForwardRule) (idx : Aesop.ForwardIndex) : Aesop.ForwardIndex

value.text:
fun r idx =>
  (if r.isConstant = true then
      pure
        { tree := idx.tree, nameToRule := Lean.PersistentHashMap.insert idx.nameToRule r.name r,
          constRules := Lean.PersistentHashSet.insert idx.constRules r }
    else
      have tree := idx.tree;
      do
      let __s ←
        forIn r.slotClusters tree fun cluster __s =>
            have tree := __s;
            do
            let __s ←
              forIn cluster tree fun slot __s =>
                  have tree := __s;
                  match slot.typeDiscrTreeKeys? with
                  | some discrTreeKeys =>
                    have tree := tree.insertKeyValue discrTreeKeys (r, slot.premiseIndex);
                    pure (ForInStep.yield tree)
                  | x => pure (ForInStep.yield tree)
            have tree : Lean.Meta.DiscrTree (Aesop.ForwardRule × Aesop.PremiseIndex) := __s
            pure (ForInStep.yield tree)
      have tree : Lean.Meta.DiscrTree (Aesop.ForwardRule × Aesop.PremiseIndex) := __s
      have nameToRule : Lean.PersistentHashMap Aesop.RuleName Aesop.ForwardRule :=
        Lean.PersistentHashMap.insert idx.nameToRule r.name r
      pure { tree := tree, nameToRule := nameToRule, constRules := idx.constRules }).run

fun rss options =>
  have result := ∅;
  do
  let simpTheorems ← Lean.Meta.getSimpTheorems
  let simprocs ← Lean.Meta.Simp.getSimprocs
  have result : Aesop.LocalRuleSet :=
    have __BaseRuleSet := ∅;
    { toBaseRuleSet := __BaseRuleSet,
      simpTheoremsArray :=
        if options.useDefaultSimpSet = true then
          (Array.mkEmpty (rss.size + 1)).push (`_, simpTheorems)
        else (Array.mkEmpty (rss.size + 1)).push (`_, { }),
      simpTheoremsArrayNonempty := ⋯,
      simprocsArray :=
        if options.useDefaultSimpSet = true then (Array.mkEmpty (rss.size + 1)).push (`_, simprocs)
        else (Array.mkEmpty (rss.size + 1)).push (`_, { }),
      simprocsArrayNonempty := ⋯, localNormSimpRules := ∅ }
  let __s ←
    forIn rss result fun x __s =>
        let result := __s;
        match x with
        | (rs, simpExtName, simprocExtName) =>
          have result :=
            have __BaseRuleSet := result.merge rs.toBaseRuleSet;
            { toBaseRuleSet := __BaseRuleSet,
              simpTheoremsArray := result.simpTheoremsArray.push (simpExtName, rs.simpTheorems),
              simpTheoremsArrayNonempty := ⋯,
              simprocsArray := result.simprocsArray.push (simprocExtName, rs.simprocs),
              simprocsArrayNonempty := ⋯, localNormSimpRules := result.localNormSimpRules };
          pure (ForInStep.yield result)
  have result : Aesop.LocalRuleSet := __s
  match Aesop.unindexPredicate? options with
    | some p => pure (result.unindex p)
    | x => pure result

    | some ns =>
      match Aesop.UnorderedArraySet.partition f.matches ns with
      | (toErase, toKeep) =>
        if toErase.isEmpty = true then pure (rs, false)
        else
          have ruleNames :=
            if toKeep.isEmpty = true then Lean.PersistentHashMap.erase rs.ruleNames f.name
            else Lean.PersistentHashMap.insert rs.ruleNames f.name toKeep;
          have erased := rs.erased;
          have unfoldRules := rs.unfoldRules;
          do
          let __s ←
            forIn toErase (erased, unfoldRules) fun r __s =>
                have erased := __s.1;
                have unfoldRules := __s.2;
                match r.builder with
                | Aesop.BuilderName.unfold =>
                  have unfoldRules := Lean.PersistentHashMap.erase unfoldRules r.name;
                  pure (ForInStep.yield (erased, unfoldRules))
                | Aesop.BuilderName.tactic =>
                  have erased := Lean.PersistentHashSet.insert erased r;
                  pure (ForInStep.yield (erased, unfoldRules))
                | Aesop.BuilderName.forward =>
                  have erased := Lean.PersistentHashSet.insert erased r;
                  pure (ForInStep.yield (erased, unfoldRules))
                | Aesop.BuilderName.destruct =>
                  have erased := Lean.PersistentHashSet.insert erased r;
                  pure (ForInStep.yield (erased, unfoldRules))
                | Aesop.BuilderName.constructors =>
                  have erased := Lean.PersistentHashSet.insert erased r;
                  pure (ForInStep.yield (erased, unfoldRules))
                | Aesop.BuilderName.cases =>
                  have erased := Lean.PersistentHashSet.insert erased r;
                  pure (ForInStep.yield (erased, unfoldRules))
                | Aesop.BuilderName.apply =>
                  have erased := Lean.PersistentHashSet.insert erased r;
                  pure (ForInStep.yield (erased, unfoldRules))
                | Aesop.BuilderName.simp => pure (ForInStep.yield (erased, unfoldRules))

          have unfoldRules : Lean.PHashMap Lean.Name (Option Lean.Name) := __s.2

Elaborates and runs the given tactic syntax `stx`. The syntax `stx` must be of
kind `tactic` or `tacticSeq`.

value.text:
fun stx =>
  Aesop.SingleRuleTac.toRuleTac fun input => do
    let preState ← Lean.saveState
    have tac : Lean.Elab.Tactic.TacticM Unit :=
      Lean.Elab.Tactic.withoutRecover (Lean.Elab.Tactic.evalTactic stx)
    let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Elab.Tactic.run input.goal tac).run'
    have postGoals : Array Lean.MVarId := __do_lift.toArray
    let postState ← Lean.saveState
    let tacticBuilder : Aesop.Script.TacticBuilder :=
      if stx.isOfKind `tactic = true then pure (Aesop.Script.Tactic.unstructured { raw := stx })
      else
        if stx.isOfKind `Lean.Parser.Tactic.tacticSeq = true then
          have stx := { raw := stx };
          (fun x => Aesop.Script.Tactic.unstructured x) <$> do
            let info ← Lean.MonadRef.mkInfoFromRefPos
            let _ ← Lean.getCurrMacroScope
            let _ ← Lean.MonadQuotation.getContext
            pure
                {
                  raw :=
                    Lean.Syntax.node3 info `Lean.Parser.Tactic.paren (Lean.Syntax.atom info "(")
                      stx.raw (Lean.Syntax.atom info ")") }
        else
          Lean.throwError
            (Lean.toMessageData "expected either a single tactic or a sequence of tactics")
    have step : Aesop.Script.LazyStep :=
      { preState := preState, preGoal := input.goal, tacticBuilders := #[tacticBuilder],
        tacticBuilders_ne := ⋯, postState := postState, postGoals := postGoals }
    let postGoals ← Array.mapM (fun x => Aesop.mvarIdToSubgoal input.goal x) postGoals
    pure (postGoals, some #[step], none)

fun decl input => do
  let tacGen ← Lean.evalConst Aesop.TacGen decl
  let initialState ← Lean.saveState
  let suggestions ← liftM (tacGen input.goal)
  let apps : Array Aesop.RuleApplication := Array.mkEmpty suggestions.size
  let errors : Array (String × Lean.Exception) := Array.mkEmpty suggestions.size
  let __s ←
    forIn suggestions (apps, errors) fun x __s =>
        let apps := __s.1;
        let errors := __s.2;
        match x with
        | (tacticStr, successProbability) => do
          liftM initialState.restore
          let env ← Lean.getEnv
          let p ←
            tryCatch
                (match Aesop.Percent.ofFloat successProbability with
                | some successProbability =>
                  match Lean.Parser.runParserCategory env `tactic tacticStr "<stdin>" with
                  | Except.ok stx => do
                    let __do_lift ←
                      liftM (Lean.Elab.Tactic.run input.goal (Lean.Elab.Tactic.evalTactic stx)).run'
                    let postGoals : Array Lean.MVarId := __do_lift.toArray
                    let postState ← Lean.saveState
                    let __do_lift ← Lean.getExprMVarAssignment? input.goal
                    have __do_jp :
                      Unit →
                        Aesop.BaseM
                          (Unit × Array Aesop.RuleApplication × Array (String × Lean.Exception)) :=
                      fun __r =>
                      let step :=
                        { preState := initialState, preGoal := input.goal,
                          tacticBuilders :=
                            #[pure (Aesop.Script.Tactic.unstructured { raw := stx })],
                          tacticBuilders_ne := ⋯, postState := postState, postGoals := postGoals };
                      do
                      let postGoals ←
                        Array.mapM (fun x => Aesop.mvarIdToSubgoal input.goal x) postGoals
                      let apps : Array Aesop.RuleApplication :=
                        apps.push
                          { goals := postGoals, postState := postState,
                            scriptSteps? := some #[step],
                            successProbability? := some successProbability }
                      pure () (apps, errors)
                    match __do_lift with
                      | some proof => do
                        let __do_lift ← Aesop.hasSorry proof
                        if __do_lift = true then do
                            let __r ←
                              Lean.throwError (Lean.toMessageData "generated proof contains sorry")
                            __do_jp __r
                          else __do_jp ()
                      | x => __do_jp ()
                  | x => do
                    let __r ←
                      Lean.throwError
                          (Lean.toMessageData "failed to parse tactic syntax" ++
                            Lean.toMessageData
                              (Lean.indentD ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) tacticStr)))
                    pure __r (apps, errors)
                | x => do
                  let __r ←
                    Lean.throwError
                        (Lean.toMessageData "invalid success probability '" ++
                            Lean.toMessageData successProbability ++
                          Lean.toMessageData "', must be between 0 and 1")
                  pure __r (apps, errors))
                fun e =>
                let errors := errors.push (tacticStr, e);
                pure () (apps, errors)
          let p : Array Aesop.RuleApplication × Array (String × Lean.Exception) := p.2
          let apps : Array Aesop.RuleApplication := p.1
          let errors : Array (String × Lean.Exception) := p.2
          pure (ForInStep.yield (apps, errors))
  let apps : Array Aesop.RuleApplication := __s.1
  let errors : Array (String × Lean.Exception) := __s.2
  have __do_jp : Unit → Aesop.BaseM Aesop.RuleTacOutput := fun __r => pure { applications := apps }
  if apps.isEmpty = true then do
      let __r ←
        Lean.throwError
            (Lean.toMessageData "Failed to apply any tactics generated. Errors:" ++
              Lean.toMessageData
                (Lean.indentD
                  (Lean.MessageData.joinSep
                    (List.map
                      (fun x =>
                        match x with
                        | (tac, e) =>
                          Lean.toMessageData tac ++ Lean.toMessageData ": " ++
                            Lean.toMessageData e.toMessageData)
                      errors.toList)
                    ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) "\n"))))
      __do_jp __r
    else __do_jp ()

doc:
Add all `let` hypotheses in the local context as `simp` theorems.

Background: by default, in the goal `x : _ := v ⊢ P[x]`, `simp` does not
substitute `x` by `v` in the target. The `simp` option `zetaDelta` can be used
to make `simp` perform this substitution, but we don't want to set it because
then Aesop `simp` would diverge from default `simp`, so we would have to adjust
the `aesop?` output as well. Instead, we add `let` hypotheses explicitly. This
way, `simp?` picks them up as well.

See lean4#3520.

fun rule input fs rs => do
  let preMetaState ←
    have this := Lean.saveState;
      liftM this
  let result? ← liftM (Aesop.runRuleTac rule.tac.run rule.name preMetaState input)
  have forwardRuleMatches : Array Aesop.ForwardRuleMatch := rule.tac.forwardRuleMatches?.getD #[]
  match result? with
    | Except.error e => do
      let __do_lift ← Aesop.TraceOption.steps.isEnabled
      have __do_jp :
        Unit →
          Aesop.NormM
            (Option (Aesop.NormRuleResult × Aesop.ForwardState × Std.HashSet Lean.FVarId) ×
              Array Aesop.ForwardRuleMatch) :=
        fun __r => pure (none, forwardRuleMatches)
      if __do_lift = true then do
          let __r ←
            Lean.addTrace Aesop.TraceOption.steps.traceClass (Lean.toMessageData e.toMessageData)
          __do_jp __r
        else __do_jp ()
    | Except.ok result =>
      match result.applications with
      | #[rapp] => do
        have this := Lean.restoreState rapp.postState;
          liftM this
        if rapp.goals.isEmpty = true then
            pure (some (Aesop.NormRuleResult.proved rapp.scriptSteps?, fs, ∅), forwardRuleMatches)
          else
            match rapp.goals with
            | #[{ diff := diff }] => do
              let fs ← liftM (Aesop.ForwardState.applyGoalDiff rs diff fs)
              have g : Lean.MVarId := diff.newGoal
              let __do_lift ← Aesop.Check.rules.isEnabled
              have __do_jp :
                Unit →
                  Aesop.NormM
                    (Option (Aesop.NormRuleResult × Aesop.ForwardState × Std.HashSet Lean.FVarId) ×
                      Array Aesop.ForwardRuleMatch) :=
                fun __r =>
                have result := Aesop.NormRuleResult.succeeded g rapp.scriptSteps?;
                pure (some (result, fs, diff.removedFVars), forwardRuleMatches)
              if __do_lift = true then
                  have mvars := Std.HashSet.ofArray input.mvars.toArray;
                  do
                  let actualMVars ← liftM (rapp.postState.runMetaM' g.getMVarDependencies)
                  if (!actualMVars == mvars) = true then do
                      let __r ←
                        liftM
                            (Aesop.runNormRuleTac.err✝ rule input
                              ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
                                "the goal produced by the rule depends on different metavariables than the original goal."))
                      __do_jp __r
                    else __do_jp ()
                else __do_jp ()
            | x =>
              liftM
                (Aesop.runNormRuleTac.err✝ rule input
                  (Lean.toMessageData "rule produced more than one subgoal."))
      | x =>
        liftM
          (Aesop.runNormRuleTac.err✝ rule input
            (Lean.toMessageData "rule did not produce exactly one rule application."))

fun {Q} gref [Aesop.Queue Q] => do

  have preGoal : Lean.MVarId := g.preNormGoal

      let rootState ← liftM Aesop.getRootMetaState
      ST.Ref.modify gref fun x =>
          Aesop.Goal.setNormalizationState (Aesop.NormalizationState.normal preGoal rootState #[]) x
      pure false
    else
      match g.normalizationState with
      | Aesop.NormalizationState.provenByNormalization postState script => pure true
      | Aesop.NormalizationState.normal postGoal postState script => pure false
      | Aesop.NormalizationState.notNormal => do
        let __do_lift ← read
        have normCtx : Aesop.NormM.Context :=
          have __src := __do_lift;
          { options := __src.options, ruleSet := __src.ruleSet,
            normSimpContext := __src.normSimpContext }
        have normState : Aesop.NormM.State :=
          { forwardState := g.forwardState, forwardRuleMatches := g.forwardRuleMatches }
        let __x ←
          Aesop.Goal.runMetaMInParentState
              (liftM
                ((ReaderT.run (Aesop.normalizeGoalMVar preGoal g.mvars) normCtx).run normState))
              g

              postState) =>
            match normResult with

                    (Aesop.Goal.setForwardState forwardState

                        (Aesop.NormalizationState.normal postGoal postState script?) g))
              pure false
            | Aesop.NormSeqResult.unchanged => do
              ST.Ref.modify gref fun x =>
                  Aesop.Goal.setNormalizationState
                    (Aesop.NormalizationState.normal preGoal postState #[]) x

              pure true

doc:
Adds a new rapp and its subgoals. If the rapp assigns mvars, all relevant
goals containing these mvars are copied as children of the rapp as well. If
the rapp drops mvars, these are treated as assigned mvars, in the sense that
the same goals are copied as if the dropped mvar had been assigned.

Note that adding a rapp may prove the parent goal, but this function does not
make the necessary changes. So after calling it, you should check whether the
rapp's parent goal is proven and mark it accordingly.

  have simprocExtName : Lean.Name :=

  discard

        simprocExtName)
  ST.Ref.modify Aesop.declaredRuleSetsRef fun rs =>
      have ruleSets := rs.ruleSets.insert rsName (ext, simpExtName, simprocExtName);
      have defaultRuleSets :=

      { ruleSets := ruleSets, defaultRuleSets := defaultRuleSets }

fun {m} [Monad m] [Lean.MonadError m] [MonadLiftT IO m] [MonadLiftT Lean.CoreM m] [Lean.MonadEnv m]
    rsf rf checkExists =>
  match rsf.matchedRuleSetNames with
  | none => do
    let __do_lift ← liftM Aesop.getDeclaredRuleSets
    let anyErased ←
      Std.HashMap.foldM (fun b rsName x => Aesop.Frontend.eraseGlobalRules.go✝ rf b rsName) false
          __do_lift
    if (checkExists && !anyErased) = true then
        Lean.throwError
          (Lean.toMessageData "'" ++ Lean.toMessageData rf.name ++
            Lean.toMessageData "' is not registered (with the given features) in any rule set.")
      else pure ()
  | some rsNames => do
    let anyErased ← Array.foldlM (Aesop.Frontend.eraseGlobalRules.go✝ rf) false rsNames
    if (checkExists && !anyErased) = true then
        Lean.throwError
          (Lean.toMessageData "'" ++ Lean.toMessageData rf.name ++
                Lean.toMessageData
                  "' is not registered (with the given features) in any of the rule sets " ++
              Lean.toMessageData (Array.map toString rsNames) ++
            Lean.toMessageData ".")
      else pure ()

    match x✝, x✝¹ with
    | Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.nil, h => h
    | h, Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.nil => h
    | s₁@h:(Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.cons r₁ a₁ n₁ t₁),

      else
        if r₂ < r₁ then
          Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.cons r₂ a₂ n₂

            else

doc:
A `HeapNode` is one of the internal nodes of the binomial heap.
It is always a perfect binary tree, with the depth of the tree stored in the `Heap`.
However the interpretation of the two pointers is different: we view the `child`
as going to the first child of this node, and `sibling` goes to the next sibling
of this tree. So it actually encodes a forest where each node has children
`node.child`, `node.child.sibling`, `node.child.sibling.sibling`, etc.

Each edge in this forest denotes a `le a b` relation that has been checked, so
the root is smaller than everything else under it.

doc:
A [binomial heap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binomial_heap) is a data structure which supports
the following primary operations:

* `insert : α → BinomialHeap α → BinomialHeap α`: add an element to the heap
* `deleteMin : BinomialHeap α → Option (α × BinomialHeap α)`:
  remove the minimum element from the heap
* `merge : BinomialHeap α → BinomialHeap α → BinomialHeap α`: combine two heaps

The first two operations are known as a "priority queue", so this could be called
a "mergeable priority queue". The standard choice for a priority queue is a binary heap,
which supports `insert` and `deleteMin` in `O(log n)`, but `merge` is `O(n)`.
With a `BinomialHeap`, all three operations are `O(log n)`.

This function detects whether the search has made progress, meaning that the
remaining goals after safe prefix expansion are different from the initial goal.
We approximate this by checking whether, after safe prefix expansion, either
of the following statements is true.

- There is a safe rapp.
- A subgoal of the preprocessing rule has been modified during normalisation.

This is an approximation because a safe rule could, in principle, leave the
initial goal unchanged.

fun {Q} [Aesop.Queue Q] completeProof =>
  Aesop.profiling
    (fun stats x elapsed =>
      { total := stats.total, configParsing := stats.configParsing,
        ruleSetConstruction := stats.ruleSetConstruction, search := stats.search,
        ruleSelection := stats.ruleSelection, script := elapsed, forwardState := stats.forwardState,
        scriptGenerated := stats.scriptGenerated, ruleStats := stats.ruleStats,
        goalStats := stats.goalStats })
    do
    let __do_lift ← read
    have options : Aesop.Options' := __do_lift.options
    if (!options.generateScript) = true then pure ()
      else
        have __do_jp := fun __x =>
          match __x with
          | (uscript, proofHasMVars) => do
            liftM uscript.checkIfEnabled
            let rootGoal ← liftM Aesop.getRootMVarId
            let rootState ← liftM Aesop.getRootMetaState
            let __do_lift ← Aesop.TraceOption.script.isEnabled
            have __do_jp : Unit → Aesop.SearchM Q Unit := fun __r => do
              let sscript? ← liftM (uscript.optimize proofHasMVars rootState rootGoal)
              Aesop.checkAndTraceScript uscript sscript? rootState rootGoal options completeProof
                  "aesop"
            if __do_lift = true then do
                let __do_lift ← liftM (uscript.renderTacticSeq rootState rootGoal)
                let __r ←
                  Lean.addTrace Aesop.TraceOption.script.traceClass
                      (Lean.toMessageData "Unstructured script:" ++
                        Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD (Lean.toMessageData __do_lift)))
                __do_jp __r
              else __do_jp ();
        if completeProof = true then do
          let __x ← liftM Aesop.extractScript
          __do_jp __x
        else do
          let __x ← liftM Aesop.extractSafePrefixScript
          __do_jp __x

fun {Q} [Aesop.Queue Q] => do
  let __do_lift ← Aesop.getTree
  have root : Aesop.MVarClusterRef := __do_lift.root
  let __do_lift ← ST.Ref.get root
  if __do_lift.state.isUnprovable = true then do
      let __do_lift ← Aesop.wasMaxRuleApplicationDepthReached
      have __do_jp : Lean.MessageData → Aesop.SearchM Q (Option Lean.MessageData) := fun msg =>
        pure (some msg)
      if __do_lift = true then do
          let __do_lift ← read
          let msg ←
            pure
                (Lean.toMessageData
                      "failed to prove the goal. Some goals were not explored because the maximum rule application depth (" ++
                    Lean.toMessageData __do_lift.options.maxRuleApplicationDepth ++
                  Lean.toMessageData
                    ") was reached. Set option 'maxRuleApplicationDepth' to increase the limit.")
          __do_jp msg
        else do
          let msg ← pure (Lean.toMessageData "failed to prove the goal after exhaustive search.")
          __do_jp msg

fun {Q} [Aesop.Queue Q] {α} mvarId remainingSafeGoals safePrefixExpansionSuccess msg? => do
  let __do_lift ← Lean.getOptions
  if Lean.Option.get __do_lift Aesop.aesop.smallErrorMessages = true then
      match msg? with
      | none => Lean.throwError (Lean.toMessageData "Tactic `aesop` failed")
      | some msg =>
        Lean.throwError (Lean.toMessageData "Tactic `aesop` failed, " ++ Lean.toMessageData msg)
    else do
      let __do_lift ← read
      have maxRapps : ℕ := __do_lift.options.maxSafePrefixRuleApplications
      have suffix : Lean.MessageData :=
        if remainingSafeGoals.isEmpty = true then Lean.toMessageData ""
        else
          have gs :=
            Lean.MessageData.joinSep (List.map Lean.toMessageData remainingSafeGoals.toList)
              ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) "\n\n");
          have suffix' :=
            if safePrefixExpansionSuccess = true then Lean.toMessageData ""
            else
              Lean.toMessageData
                    "\nThe safe prefix was not fully expanded because the maximum number of rule applications (" ++
                  Lean.toMessageData maxRapps ++
                Lean.toMessageData ") was reached.";
          Lean.toMessageData "\nRemaining goals after safe rules:" ++
              Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD gs) ++
            Lean.toMessageData suffix'
      match msg? with
        | none =>
          Lean.throwError
            (Lean.toMessageData "Tactic `aesop` failed\nInitial goal:" ++
                Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD (Lean.MessageData.ofGoal mvarId)) ++
              Lean.toMessageData suffix)
        | some msg =>
          Lean.throwError
            (Lean.toMessageData "Tactic `aesop` failed, " ++ Lean.toMessageData msg ++
                  Lean.toMessageData "\nInitial goal:" ++
                Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD (Lean.MessageData.ofGoal mvarId)) ++
              Lean.toMessageData suffix)

`aesop <clause>*` tries to solve the current goal by applying a set of rules
registered with the `@[aesop]` attribute. See [its
README](https://github.com/JLimperg/aesop#readme) for a tutorial and a

clauses are:

  an integer for safe and norm rules. `<rule>` is the name of a declaration or

  `Aesop.Options`.

  `simp` rule. The given options are directly passed to `simp`. For example,
  `(simp_config := { zeta := false })` makes Aesop use

fun rs c goal =>
  have rs := rs;
  do
  let __s ←
    forIn c.additionalRules rs fun ruleExpr __s =>
        have rs := __s;
        do
        let rules ← Aesop.Frontend.RuleExpr.buildAdditionalLocalRules goal ruleExpr
        let __s ←
          forIn rules rs fun rule __s =>
              have rs := __s;
              have rs := rs.add rule;
              pure (ForInStep.yield rs)
        have rs : Aesop.LocalRuleSet := __s
        pure (ForInStep.yield rs)
  have rs : Aesop.LocalRuleSet := __s
  let __s ←
    forIn c.erasedRules rs fun ruleExpr __s =>
        have rs := __s;
        do
        let filters ←
          Aesop.ElabM.run (Aesop.ElabM.Context.forErasing goal) ruleExpr.toLocalRuleFilters
        let __s ←
          forIn filters rs fun rFilter __s =>
              have rs := __s;
              match rs.erase rFilter with
              | (rs', anyErased) =>
                have rs := rs';
                if (!anyErased) = true then do
                  Lean.throwError
                      (Lean.toMessageData "aesop: '" ++ Lean.toMessageData rFilter.name ++
                        Lean.toMessageData
                          "' is not registered (with the given features) in any rule set.")
                  pure (ForInStep.yield rs)
                else pure (ForInStep.yield rs)
        have rs : Aesop.LocalRuleSet := __s
        pure (ForInStep.yield rs)
  have rs : Aesop.LocalRuleSet := __s
  pure rs

fun stx goal =>

    (fun s x t =>
      { total := t, configParsing := s.configParsing, ruleSetConstruction := s.ruleSetConstruction,
        search := s.search, ruleSelection := s.ruleSelection, script := s.script,
        forwardState := s.forwardState, scriptGenerated := s.scriptGenerated,
        ruleStats := s.ruleStats, goalStats := s.goalStats })
    do
    let config ←
      Aesop.profiling
          (fun s x t =>
            { total := s.total, configParsing := t, ruleSetConstruction := s.ruleSetConstruction,
              search := s.search, ruleSelection := s.ruleSelection, script := s.script,
              forwardState := s.forwardState, scriptGenerated := s.scriptGenerated,
              ruleStats := s.ruleStats, goalStats := s.goalStats })
          (liftM (Aesop.Frontend.TacticConfig.parse stx goal))
    let ruleSet ←
      Aesop.profiling
          (fun s x t =>
            { total := s.total, configParsing := s.configParsing, ruleSetConstruction := t,
              search := s.search, ruleSelection := s.ruleSelection, script := s.script,
              forwardState := s.forwardState, scriptGenerated := s.scriptGenerated,
              ruleStats := s.ruleStats, goalStats := s.goalStats })
          (liftM (Aesop.Frontend.TacticConfig.getRuleSet goal config))
    Aesop.withConstAesopTraceNode Aesop.TraceOption.ruleSet
        (pure ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) "Rule set"))
        (liftM (ruleSet.trace Aesop.TraceOption.ruleSet))
    Aesop.profiling
        (fun s x t =>
          { total := s.total, configParsing := s.configParsing,
            ruleSetConstruction := s.ruleSetConstruction, search := t,
            ruleSelection := s.ruleSelection, script := s.script, forwardState := s.forwardState,
            scriptGenerated := s.scriptGenerated, ruleStats := s.ruleStats,
            goalStats := s.goalStats })
        do
        let __do_lift ← Aesop.getStats
        let __x ←
          liftM
              (Aesop.search goal (some ruleSet) config.options config.simpConfig
                config.simpConfigSyntax? __do_lift)
        match __x with
          | (goals, stats) =>
            have solved := goals.isEmpty;
            do
            liftM (Lean.Elab.Tactic.replaceMainGoal goals.toList)
            Aesop.modifyStats fun x => stats
            pure solved

def Aesop.StatsReport.scriptsCore (nSlowest : ℕ := 30) (nontrivialOnly : Bool := false) :
  Aesop.StatsReport

value.text:
fun nSlowest nontrivialOnly statsArray =>
  (have statsArray :=
      if nontrivialOnly = true then
        Array.filter
          (fun x =>
            match x.stats.scriptGenerated with
            | none => false
            | some g => g.hasMVar)
          statsArray
      else statsArray;
    have staticallyStructured := 0;
    have perfectlyStaticallyStructured := 0;
    have dynamicallyStructured := 0;
    have perfectlyDynamicallyStructured := 0;
    have totalTimes := Array.mkEmpty statsArray.size;
    have scriptTimes := Array.mkEmpty statsArray.size;
    do
    let __s ←
      forIn statsArray
          (staticallyStructured, perfectlyStaticallyStructured, dynamicallyStructured,
            perfectlyDynamicallyStructured, totalTimes, scriptTimes)
          fun stats __s =>
          have staticallyStructured := __s.1;
          have __s := __s.2;
          have perfectlyStaticallyStructured := __s.1;
          have __s := __s.2;
          have dynamicallyStructured := __s.1;
          have __s := __s.2;
          have perfectlyDynamicallyStructured := __s.1;
          have __s := __s.2;
          have totalTimes := __s.1;
          have scriptTimes := __s.2;
          have stats := stats.stats;
          have totalTimes := totalTimes.push stats.total;
          match stats.scriptGenerated with
          | none =>
            pure
              (ForInStep.yield
                (staticallyStructured, perfectlyStaticallyStructured, dynamicallyStructured,
                  perfectlyDynamicallyStructured, totalTimes, scriptTimes))
          | some g =>
            have scriptTimes := scriptTimes.push stats.script;
            match g.method with
            | Aesop.ScriptGenerated.Method.static =>
              have staticallyStructured := staticallyStructured + 1;
              if g.perfect = true then
                have perfectlyStaticallyStructured := perfectlyStaticallyStructured + 1;
                pure
                  (ForInStep.yield
                    (staticallyStructured, perfectlyStaticallyStructured, dynamicallyStructured,
                      perfectlyDynamicallyStructured, totalTimes, scriptTimes))
              else
                pure
                  (ForInStep.yield
                    (staticallyStructured, perfectlyStaticallyStructured, dynamicallyStructured,
                      perfectlyDynamicallyStructured, totalTimes, scriptTimes))
            | Aesop.ScriptGenerated.Method.dynamic =>
              have dynamicallyStructured := dynamicallyStructured + 1;
              if g.perfect = true then
                have perfectlyDynamicallyStructured := perfectlyDynamicallyStructured + 1;
                pure
                  (ForInStep.yield
                    (staticallyStructured, perfectlyStaticallyStructured, dynamicallyStructured,
                      perfectlyDynamicallyStructured, totalTimes, scriptTimes))
              else
                pure
                  (ForInStep.yield
                    (staticallyStructured, perfectlyStaticallyStructured, dynamicallyStructured,
                      perfectlyDynamicallyStructured, totalTimes, scriptTimes))
    have staticallyStructured : ℕ := __s.1
    have __s : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ × Array Aesop.Nanos × Array Aesop.Nanos := __s.2
    have perfectlyStaticallyStructured : ℕ := __s.1
    have __s : ℕ × ℕ × Array Aesop.Nanos × Array Aesop.Nanos := __s.2
    have dynamicallyStructured : ℕ := __s.1
    have __s : ℕ × Array Aesop.Nanos × Array Aesop.Nanos := __s.2
    have perfectlyDynamicallyStructured : ℕ := __s.1
    have __s : Array Aesop.Nanos × Array Aesop.Nanos := __s.2
    have totalTimes : Array Aesop.Nanos := __s.1
    have scriptTimes : Array Aesop.Nanos := __s.2
    have slowest : Array Aesop.StatsExtensionEntry :=
      statsArray.qsort fun s₁ s₂ => decide (s₁.stats.script > s₂.stats.script)
    have slowest : Array Aesop.StatsExtensionEntry :=
      Std.Slice.toArray (slowest.toSubarray 0 nSlowest)
    have nSlowest : ℕ := min slowest.size nSlowest
    have slowestFmt : Array Std.Format :=
      Array.map
        (fun e =>
          have pos :=
            match e.position? with
            | some pos => Std.format pos.line ++ Std.format ":" ++ Std.format pos.column
            | none => Std.format "?:?";
          Std.format e.fileName ++ Std.format ":" ++ Std.format pos ++ Std.format ": script " ++
                    Std.format e.stats.script ++
                  Std.format ", total " ++
                Std.format e.stats.total ++
              Std.format ", type " ++
            Std.format (Aesop.StatsReport.scriptsCore.fmtScriptGenerated✝ e.stats.scriptGenerated))
        slowest
    Std.format "Statistics for " ++ Std.format statsArray.size ++ Std.format " Aesop calls" ++
                              Std.format
                                (if nontrivialOnly = true then
                                  Std.format " with nontrivial script generation"
                                else Std.Format.text "") ++
                            Std.format
                              " in current and imported modules\nTotal Aesop time:         " ++
                          Std.format (Aesop.StatsReport.scriptsCore.fmtTimes✝ totalTimes) ++
                        Std.format "\nScript generation time:   " ++
                      Std.format (Aesop.StatsReport.scriptsCore.fmtTimes✝ scriptTimes) ++
                    Std.format "\nScripts generated:        " ++
                  Std.format scriptTimes.size ++
                Std.format "\n- Statically  structured: " ++
              Std.format staticallyStructured ++
            Std.format "\n" ++
          (Std.format "  - perfectly:            " ++ Std.format perfectlyStaticallyStructured ++
                Std.format "\n- Dynamically structured: " ++
              Std.format dynamicallyStructured ++
            Std.format "\n") ++
        (Std.format "  - perfectly:            " ++ Std.format perfectlyDynamicallyStructured ++
                Std.format "\n\n" ++
              Std.format nSlowest ++
            Std.format " Aesop calls with slowest script generation:\n" ++
          Std.format (Std.Format.joinSep slowestFmt.toList (Std.Format.text "\n")))).run

fun {α} goal mvars preState matchResult =>
  Lean.withTraceNode `saturate
    (fun x => pure (Lean.toMessageData "running rule " ++ Lean.toMessageData matchResult.rule.name))
    (Aesop.profilingRule (Aesop.DisplayRuleName.ruleName matchResult.rule.name) (fun x => x.isSome)
      do
      let __do_lift ← read
      have input : Aesop.RuleTacInput :=
        { goal := goal, mvars := mvars, indexMatchLocations := matchResult.locations,
          patternSubsts? := matchResult.patternSubsts?, options := __do_lift.options }
      let tacResult ←
        liftM (Aesop.runRuleTac matchResult.rule.tac.run matchResult.rule.name preState input)
      match tacResult with
        | Except.error exc =>
          have cls := `saturate;
          do
          let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
          have __do_jp :
            Unit →
              Aesop.SaturateM (Option (Aesop.GoalDiff × Option (Array Aesop.Script.LazyStep))) :=
            fun __r => pure none
          if __do_lift = true then do
              let __r ← Lean.addTrace cls exc.toMessageData
              __do_jp __r
            else __do_jp ()
        | Except.ok output => do
          let __x ← Aesop.getSingleGoal output
          match __x with
            | (diff, postState, scriptSteps?) => do
              liftM postState.restore
              pure (some (diff, scriptSteps?)))

Given `rhss` the right-hand-sides of a `match`-syntax notation,
We tag them with fresh identifiers `alt_idx`. We use them to detect whether an alternative
has been used or not.
The result is a triple `(altIdxMap, ignoreIfUnused, rhssNew)` where
- `altIdxMap` is a mapping from the `alt_idx` identifiers to right-hand-side indices.
  That is, the map contains the entry `alt_idx ↦ i` if `alt_idx` was used to mark `rhss[i]`.
- `i ∈ ignoreIfUnused` if `rhss[i]` is marked with `no_error_if_unused%`
- `rhssNew` is the updated array of right-hand-sides.

  match __x with
    | (stx, used) => do
      forIn' (*...alts.size) PUnit.unit fun i h __s =>
          if (Std.HashSet.contains used i || Std.HashSet.contains ignoreIfUnused i) = true then

          else do

            pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)

doc:
Represents information about what control effects a `do` block has.

The fields split by flavor:

* `breaks`, `continues`, `returnsEarly`, and `reassigns` are **syntactic**: `true`/non-empty iff
  the corresponding construct appears anywhere in the source text of the block, independent of
  whether it is semantically reachable. Downstream elaborators must assume every such syntactic
  effect may occur, because the elaborator visits every doElem (only top-level
  `return`/`break`/`continue` short-circuit via `elabAsSyntacticallyDeadCode`).
* `numRegularExits` is also **syntactic**: the number of times the block wires the enclosing
  continuation into its elaborated expression. `withDuplicableCont` reads it as a join-point
  duplication trigger (`> 1`).
* `noFallthrough = true` asserts that the next doElem in the enclosing sequence is semantically
  irrelevant (control never falls through to it). `noFallthrough = false` makes no such
  assertion. The dead-code warning fires on the next element when this is `true`.

Invariant: `numRegularExits = 0 → noFallthrough`. The converse does not hold.

fun es u =>
  if h : es.size > 0 then
    have tuple := es.back h;
    do
    let tupleTy ← Lean.Meta.inferType tuple
    let u ← Lean.Meta.getDecLevel tupleTy
    have es : Array Lean.Expr := es.pop
    let __s ←
      forIn (0...es.size) (tuple, tupleTy, u, es) fun i __s =>
          have tuple := __s.1;
          have __s := __s.2;
          have tupleTy := __s.1;
          have __s := __s.2;
          have u := __s.1;
          have es := __s.2;
          have e := es.back!;
          do
          let ty ← Lean.Meta.inferType e
          let u' ← Lean.Meta.getDecLevel ty
          have tuple : Lean.Expr := Lean.mkApp4 (Lean.mkConst `Prod.mk [u', u]) ty tupleTy e tuple
          have tupleTy : Lean.Expr := Lean.mkApp2 (Lean.mkConst `Prod [u', u]) ty tupleTy
          have u : Lean.Level := (Lean.mkLevelMax u u').normalize
          have es : Array Lean.Expr := es.pop
          pure (ForInStep.yield (tuple, tupleTy, u, es))
    have tuple : Lean.Expr := __s.1
    have __s : Lean.Expr × Lean.Level × Array Lean.Expr := __s.2
    have tupleTy : Lean.Expr := __s.1
    pure (tuple, tupleTy)
  else
    pure (Lean.mkConst `PUnit.unit [Lean.mkLevelSucc u], Lean.mkConst `PUnit [Lean.mkLevelSucc u])

doc:
Given a continuation `dec`, a reference `ref`, and an element result type `elementType`, returns a
continuation derived from `dec` with result type `elementType`.
If `dec` already has result type `elementType`, simply returns `dec`.
Otherwise, an error is logged and a new continuation is returned that calls `dec` with `sorry` as a
result. The error is reported at `ref`.

fun dec ref elementType => do
  let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.isDefEqGuarded dec.resultType elementType)
  if __do_lift = true then pure dec
    else
      have errMessage := Lean.Elab.Do.mkMonadicResultTypeMismatchError dec.resultType elementType;
      do
      let __do_lift ← readThe Lean.Elab.Term.Context
      have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.Elab.Do.DoElabM Lean.Elab.Do.DoElemCont := fun __r => do
        Lean.logErrorAt ref errMessage
        let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.mkFreshUserName `__r)
        pure
            { resultName := __do_lift, resultType := elementType,
              k := do
                let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.mkSorry dec.resultType true)
                Lean.Meta.mapLetDecl dec.resultName dec.resultType __do_lift (fun x => dec.k) true
                    Lean.LocalDeclKind.implDetail,
              kind := dec.kind }
      if __do_lift.errToSorry = true then __do_jp ()
        else do
          let __r ← Lean.throwErrorAt ref errMessage
          __do_jp __r

doc:
Call `caller` with a duplicable proxy of `dec`.
When the proxy is elaborated more than once, a join point is introduced so that `dec` is only
elaborated once to fill in the RHS of this join point.

This is useful for control-flow constructs like `if` and `match`, where multiple tail-called
branches share the continuation.

signature.text:
def Lean.Elab.Do.DoElemCont.withDuplicableCont (nondupDec : Lean.Elab.Do.DoElemCont)
  (callerInfo : Lean.Elab.Do.ControlInfo)
  (caller : Lean.Elab.Do.DoElemCont → Lean.Elab.Do.DoElabM Lean.Expr) :
  Lean.Elab.Do.DoElabM Lean.Expr

value.text:
fun nondupDec callerInfo caller =>
  if
      (match nondupDec.kind with
        | Lean.Elab.Do.DoElemContKind.duplicable => true
        | x => false) =
        true then
    caller nondupDec
  else do
    let __do_lift ← read
    have γ : Lean.Expr := __do_lift.doBlockResultType
    let mγ ← Lean.Elab.Do.mkMonadApp γ
    let __do_lift ← read
    have mutVars : Array Lean.Elab.Do.MutVar :=
      Array.filter (fun x => callerInfo.reassigns.contains x.getId) __do_lift.mutVars
    have mutVarNames : Array Lean.Name := Array.map (fun x => x.getId) mutVars
    let joinName ← liftM (Lean.mkFreshUserName `__do_jp)
    let mutDecls ← Array.mapM (fun x => liftM (Lean.Meta.getLocalDeclFromUserName x)) mutVarNames
    have mutTypes : Array Lean.Expr := Array.map (fun x => x.type) mutDecls
    let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.mkArrowN mutTypes mγ)
    let joinTy ← liftM (Lean.mkArrow nondupDec.resultType __do_lift)
    let joinRhsMVar ← liftM (Lean.Meta.mkFreshExprSyntheticOpaqueMVar joinTy)
    Lean.Meta.withLetDecl joinName joinTy joinRhsMVar
        (fun jp =>
          have mkJump := do
            let jp' ← liftM (Lean.Meta.getFVarFromUserName joinName)
            let result ← liftM (Lean.Meta.getFVarFromUserName nondupDec.resultName)
            have e : Lean.Expr := Lean.mkApp jp' result
            let __s ←
              forIn mutVars e fun x __s =>
                  have e := __s;
                  do
                  let newX ← liftM (Lean.Meta.getFVarFromUserName x.getId)
                  liftM (Lean.Elab.Term.addTermInfo' x.ident.raw newX)
                  let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.getFVarFromUserName x.getId)
                  have e : Lean.Expr := Lean.mkApp e __do_lift
                  pure (ForInStep.yield e)
            have e : Lean.Expr := __s
            pure e;
          have elabBody :=
            caller
              { resultName := nondupDec.resultName, resultType := nondupDec.resultType, k := mkJump,
                kind := Lean.Elab.Do.DoElemContKind.duplicable };
          do
          let body? ← Lean.Elab.Do.observingPostpone elabBody
          let joinRhs ←
            joinRhsMVar.mvarId!.withContext
                (Lean.Meta.withLocalDeclD nondupDec.resultName nondupDec.resultType fun r =>
                  Lean.Meta.withLocalDeclsDND (Array.map (fun d => (d.userName, d.type)) mutDecls)
                    fun muts => do
                    forIn (mutVars.zip muts) PUnit.unit fun x __s =>
                        match x with
                        | (x, newX) => do
                          liftM (Lean.Elab.Term.addTermInfo' x.ident.raw newX)
                          pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
                    let e ← (nondupDec.withDeadCodeFromInfo callerInfo).k
                    liftM (Lean.Meta.mkLambdaFVars (#[r] ++ muts) e))
          let __do_lift ← liftM (joinRhsMVar.mvarId!.checkedAssign joinRhs)
          have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.Elab.Do.DoElabM Lean.Expr := fun __r => do
            let body ←
              body?.getDM
                  (Lean.Elab.Do.doElabToSyntax
                    ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) "join point RHS") elabBody fun x =>
                    liftM (Lean.Elab.Term.postponeElabTerm x.raw (some mγ)))
            if callerInfo.numRegularExits > 1 then
                liftM (Lean.Meta.mkLetFVars #[jp] body true false)
              else do
                let __do_lift ← liftM (body.abstractM #[jp])
                pure (__do_lift.instantiateBetaRevRange 0 1 #[joinRhs])
          if __do_lift = true then __do_jp ()
            else do
              let __r ←
                joinRhsMVar.mvarId!.withContext
                    (Lean.throwError
                      (Lean.toMessageData
                              "Bug in a `do` elaborator. Failed to assign join point RHS" ++
                            Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentExpr joinRhs) ++
                          Lean.toMessageData "\nto metavariable\n" ++
                        Lean.toMessageData joinRhsMVar.mvarId!))
              __do_jp __r)
        true Lean.LocalDeclKind.implDetail

value.text:
fun {α} rootCtx childCtx tunneledVars =>
  have tunnelDecls := childCtx.findFromUserNames tunneledVars rootCtx.numIndices;
  do
  let fvars ←
    (fun x => x.2.fvarIds) <$> (Array.mapM (fun x => x.type.collectFVars) tunnelDecls).run { }
  let fvarDecls ← Array.mapM (fun x => x.getDecl) fvars
  have fvarDecls : Array Lean.LocalDecl :=
    (Array.takeWhile (fun x => decide (x.index ≥ rootCtx.numIndices))
        (fvarDecls.insertionSort fun x1 x2 => decide (x1.index > x2.index))).reverse
  have tunnelDecls : Array Lean.LocalDecl :=
    Array.filter (fun tun => !fvarDecls.any fun x => x.index == tun.index) tunnelDecls
  have tunnelDecls : Array Lean.LocalDecl := fvarDecls ++ tunnelDecls
  have rootCtx : Lean.LocalContext := rootCtx
  let __s ←
    forIn tunnelDecls rootCtx fun decl __s =>
        have rootCtx := __s;
        have rootCtx := rootCtx.addDecl (decl.setNondep true);
        pure (ForInStep.yield rootCtx)
  have rootCtx : Lean.LocalContext := __s
  pure rootCtx

doc:
Elaboration of a `do` block `do $e; $rest`, results in a call
``elabTerm `(do $e; $rest) = elabDoElem e dec``, where `elabDoElem e ·` is the elaborator for `do`
element `e`, and `dec` is the `DoElemCont` describing the elaboration of the rest of the block
`rest`.

If the semantics of `e` resumes its continuation `rest`, its elaborator must bind its result to
`resultName`, ensure that it has type `resultType` and then elaborate `rest` using `dec`.

Clearly, for term elements `e : m α`, the result has type `α`.
More subtly, for binding elements `let x := e` or `let x ← e`, the result has type `PUnit` and is
unrelated to the type of the bound variable `x`.

Examples:
* `return` drops the continuation; `return x; pure ()` elaborates to `pure x`.
* `let x ← e; rest x` elaborates to `e >>= fun x => rest x`.
* `let x := 3; let y ← (let x ← e); rest x` elaborates to
  `let x := 3; e >>= fun x_1 => let y := (); rest x`, which is immediately zeta-reduced to
  `let x := 3; e >>= fun x_1 => rest x`.
* `one; two` elaborates to `one >>= fun (_ : PUnit) => two`; it is an error if `one` does not have
  type `PUnit`.

doc:
Restores the local context to `oldCtx` and adds the new reaching definitions of the mut vars and
result. Then resume the continuation `k` with the `mutVars` restored to the given `oldMutVars`.

This function is useful to de-nest
```
let mut x := 0
let y := 3
let z ← do
  let mut y ← e
  x := y + 1
  pure y
let y := y + 3
pure (x + y + z)
```
into
```
let mut x := 0
let y := 3
let mut y† ← e
x := y† + 1
let z ← pure y†
let y := y + 3
pure (x + y + z)
```
Note that the continuation of the `let z ← ...` bind, roughly
``k := .cont `z _ `(let y := y + 3; pure (x + y + z))``,
needs to be elaborated in a local context that contains the reassignment of `x`, but not the shadowing
mut var definition of `y`.

  have oldMutVars := oldCtx.mutVars;
  have oldMutVarDefs := oldCtx.mutVarDefs;
  have tunneledDefs := oldMutVarDefs.insert resultName default;
  do
  let __do_lift ← Lean.getLCtx
  let newCtx ← liftM (Lean.Elab.Do.addReachingDefsAsNonDep✝ oldLCtx __do_lift tunneledDefs)
  Lean.Meta.withLCtx' newCtx
      (withReader
        (fun ctx =>
          { monadInfo := ctx.monadInfo, mutVars := oldMutVars, mutVarDefs := oldMutVarDefs,
            doBlockResultType := ctx.doBlockResultType, contInfo := ctx.contInfo,
            deadCode := ctx.deadCode, ops := ctx.ops })

def Lean.Elab.Do.EffectForwarder.ofCont (info : Lean.Elab.Do.ControlInfo)
  (dec : Lean.Elab.Do.DoElemCont) : Lean.Elab.Do.DoElabM Lean.Elab.Do.EffectForwarder

value.text:
fun info dec => do
  let __do_lift ← read
  have mi : Lean.Elab.Do.MonadInfo := __do_lift.monadInfo
  let __do_lift ← read
  have reassignedMutVars : Array Lean.Elab.Do.MutVar :=
    Array.filter (fun x => info.reassigns.contains x.getId) __do_lift.mutVars
  have reassignedMutVarNames : Array Lean.Name := Array.map (fun x => x.getId) reassignedMutVars
  let __do_lift ← Lean.Elab.Do.getReturnCont
  have ρ : Lean.Expr := __do_lift.resultType
  let __do_lift ←
    Array.mapM (fun x => Lean.LocalDecl.type <$> liftM (Lean.Meta.getLocalDeclFromUserName x))
        reassignedMutVarNames
  let σ ← liftM (Lean.Meta.mkProdN __do_lift mi.u)
  have needEarlyReturn : Option Lean.Expr := if info.returnsEarly = true then some ρ else none
  let __do_lift ← Lean.Elab.Do.getBreakCont
  have needBreak : Bool := info.breaks && __do_lift.isSome
  let __do_lift ← Lean.Elab.Do.getContinueCont
  have needContinue : Bool := info.continues && __do_lift.isSome
  have needState : Option (Array Lean.Elab.Do.MutVar × Lean.Expr) :=
    if reassignedMutVars.isEmpty = true then none else some (reassignedMutVars, σ)
  have returnBase? : Option Lean.Elab.Do.ControlStack := none
  have breakBase? : Option Lean.Elab.Do.ControlStack := none
  have continueBase? : Option Lean.Elab.Do.ControlStack := none
  have controlStack : Lean.Elab.Do.ControlStack := Lean.Elab.Do.ControlStack.base mi
  have __do_jp :
    Unit →
      Option Lean.Elab.Do.ControlStack →
        Lean.Elab.Do.ControlStack → Lean.Elab.Do.DoElabM Lean.Elab.Do.EffectForwarder :=
    fun __r returnBase? controlStack =>
    have __do_jp := fun __r controlStack =>
      have __do_jp := fun __r breakBase? controlStack =>
        have __do_jp := fun __r continueBase? controlStack => do
          let __do_lift ← controlStack.stM dec.resultType
          pure
              { origCont := dec, returnBase? := returnBase?, breakBase? := breakBase?,
                continueBase? := continueBase?, liftedStack := controlStack,
                liftedDoBlockResultType := __do_lift };
        if needContinue = true then
          have continueBase? := some controlStack;
          have controlStack := Lean.Elab.Do.ControlStack.continueT mi controlStack;
          __do_jp () continueBase? controlStack
        else __do_jp () continueBase? controlStack;
      if needBreak = true then
        have breakBase? := some controlStack;
        have controlStack := Lean.Elab.Do.ControlStack.breakT mi controlStack;
        __do_jp () breakBase? controlStack
      else __do_jp () breakBase? controlStack;
    match needState with
    | some (reassignedMutVars, σ) =>
      have controlStack := Lean.Elab.Do.ControlStack.stateT mi reassignedMutVars σ controlStack;
      __do_jp () controlStack
    | x => __do_jp () controlStack
  match needEarlyReturn with
    | some ρ =>
      have returnBase? := some controlStack;
      have controlStack := Lean.Elab.Do.ControlStack.earlyReturnT mi ρ controlStack;
      __do_jp () returnBase? controlStack
    | x => __do_jp () returnBase? controlStack

  (optionTWrapper casesOnWrapper : Lean.Name)
  (getCont : Lean.Elab.Do.DoElabM (Lean.Elab.Do.DoElabM Lean.Expr))
  (base : Lean.Elab.Do.ControlStack) : Lean.Elab.Do.ControlStack

value.text:
fun baseMonadInfo optionTWrapper casesOnWrapper getCont base =>
  {
    description := fun x =>
      Lean.toMessageData "OptionT over " ++ Lean.toMessageData (base.description ()),
    m := do
      let __do_lift ← base.m
      pure (Lean.mkApp (Lean.mkConst optionTWrapper [baseMonadInfo.u, baseMonadInfo.v]) __do_lift),
    stM := base.stM ∘ Lean.Elab.Do.ControlStack.optionT.stM✝ baseMonadInfo,
    runInBase := fun e => do
      let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.mkAppM `OptionT.run #[e])
      base.runInBase __do_lift,
    restoreCont := fun dec => do
      let resultName ← liftM (Lean.mkFreshUserName `e)
      have resultType : Lean.Expr :=
        Lean.Elab.Do.ControlStack.optionT.stM✝ baseMonadInfo dec.resultType
      have k : Lean.Elab.Do.DoElabM Lean.Expr := do
        let e ← liftM (Lean.Meta.getFVarFromUserName resultName)
        let outerCont ← getCont
        let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.mkFreshUserName `r)
        let kexit ←
          Lean.Meta.withLocalDeclD __do_lift (Lean.mkConst `Unit) fun r => do
              let __do_lift ← outerCont
              liftM (Lean.Meta.mkLambdaFVars #[r] __do_lift)
        let ksuccess ←
          Lean.Meta.withLocalDeclD dec.resultName dec.resultType fun r => do
              let __do_lift ← dec.k
              liftM (Lean.Meta.mkLambdaFVars #[r] __do_lift)
        let __do_lift ← read
        let β ← Lean.Elab.Do.mkMonadApp __do_lift.doBlockResultType
        pure
            (Lean.mkApp5 (Lean.mkConst casesOnWrapper [baseMonadInfo.u, baseMonadInfo.v])
              dec.resultType β e kexit ksuccess)
      base.restoreCont { resultName := resultName, resultType := resultType, k := k } }
